subject: Re: Order Form — request for pricing floor exception and annualization deferment
messages:
From: Emma L. Harper <emma.harper@stellarishealth.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood-inference.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form questions — floor and annualization request

Hi Irene —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're excited to move forward but need to resolve two commercial points before procurement will sign the order form attached.

1) Annualization window: Our business is heavily seasonal (Q3 is typically our trough). The order form's quarterly minimums will trigger before we ramp. Can we defer the annualization window start date until Oct 1, 2027 (effectively shifting the first 12-month measurement period) so our first partial year isn't penalized?

2) Pricing floor: Given the seasonality, can Redwood agree to a temporary suspension of the pricing floor for the first 3 billing cycles while we onboard and run pilots? We would still true-up usage at the end of the 12-month window.

I've attached our draft Order Form (v2) and a projected ramp spreadsheet. Procurement has asked that any exception be documented in the Pricing Exhibit or as an annex to the Order Form.

Can you loop in legal and finance? We appreciate a short written path we can share internally.

—Emma
Director of Product, Stellaris Health
Attachment: Stellaris_OrderForm_v2.pdf

From: irene_choi@redwood-inference.com
To: Emma L. Harper <emma.harper@stellarishealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com, marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — floor and annualization request

Emma —

Thanks for the clear note and the order-form draft. Looping in Karthik (commercial) and Marissa (legal) to propose options. High level — we generally support business-friendly onboarding concessions when tied to a documented mutual action plan. Two things we'll need to verify with finance/legal:

- Exact wording for a temporary floor suspension (explicit duration + true-up mechanics).
- Whether the annualization window can be shifted formally or we should add an early-year carve-out to the first 12-month calculation.

Karthik / Marissa: please propose language that (1) protects Redwood's commitment economics, (2) limits exposure (cap on any temporary credit or surcharge), and (3) is acceptable to the customer counsel.

Irene
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com
To: Emma L. Harper <emma.harper@stellarishealth.com>, irene_choi@redwood-inference.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed commercial approach — annualization and temporary floor suspension

Emma / team —

Thanks for the patience. Based on your ramp and our internal review, here's a commercial compromise that should be acceptable to both sides:

1) Annualization deferment — Redwood will set the "Measurement Start Date" for the Pricing Exhibit to Oct 1, 2027 for the purposes of calculating the annualized committed volume for the first contract year only. After that, normal 12-month trailing calculation applies.

2) Temporary floor suspension — Redwood will waive the hard pricing floor for the first three billing cycles (defined in the Order Form as the first 3 consecutive months following Service Activation) provided the customer meets the mutual onboarding milestones in Appendix A (pilot completion, data transfer, and production readiness).

3) Surcharge / true-up cap — If the customer fails to meet the annualized commitment at true-up, Redwood retains the right to apply a true-up surcharge; however, for this instance the surcharge shall be capped at 5% of the shortfall charge (not to exceed $25,000 in aggregate for year one).

4) Credits escrow — To address procurement concerns, Redwood will place a one-time credit hold of $10,000 that will be applied at true-up or refunded pro-rata if the annualized commit is met.

If commercial looks good to you, Marissa will circulate a tracked-change Pricing Exhibit to reflect the above. Please note: all concessions are contingent on signing the final Order Form and Appendix A (mutual action plan) within 30 days.

Best —
Karthik
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
To: Emma L. Harper <emma.harper@stellarishealth.com>, Tom Nguyen <t.nguyen@stellarishealth.com>, irene_choi@redwood-inference.com, karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Pricing Exhibit redline (tracked)

Emma / Tom —

Attached is a tracked-change redline to the Pricing Exhibit (Pricing_Exhibit_redline_20270606.docx) implementing Karthik's commercial points. Highlights of edits and rationale: 

- Section 2(b): "Measurement Start Date" set to October 1, 2027 for the initial 12-month measurement period; language automatically reverts to standard measurement for subsequent years.
- Section 3(a) (Pricing Floor): temporary suspension clause added with explicit "three (3) consecutive billing cycles" duration and reference to Appendix A milestones.
- Section 3(c) (True-up and Surcharges): added surcharge cap (5% of calculated shortfall charge) and maximum aggregate exposure for year one ($25,000).
- Section 5: credit hold mechanics and refund timing on true-up.

Open items for negotiation from our side: (A) escrow mechanics (we propose Redwood retains the credit until true-up, refund if commit met), and (B) liability / indemnity interaction with any credit refunds — procurement often asks to tie credits to performance; we usually avoid linking to indemnity language.

Please review and provide trackable countered edits if needed. If Stellaris legal can mark up the attached, we'll iterate quickly.

Attachment: Pricing_Exhibit_redline_20270606.docx

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Nguyen <t.nguyen@stellarishealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com, Emma L. Harper <emma.harper@stellarishealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com, irene_choi@redwood-inference.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 13:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing Exhibit redline (tracked)

Team —

Thanks for the redline. Stellaris legal can accept some of the proposed language but we have two material counterpoints: 

1) Duration of suspension — we can agree to a 3-month operational suspension for the floor, but we request an additional 1-month buffer (i.e., 4 months total) if onboarding milestones are met within the first 90 days but production cutover slips by no fault of Stellaris (e.g., vendor delays). That buffer would be automatic if Appendix A milestones are reasonably documented.

2) Surcharge cap — 5% is acceptable as a floor, but we cannot agree to the $25,000 hard cap; given our volume profile the dollar cap would be insufficient protection on very large deals. We propose a tiered cap: $25,000 for customers with first-year ARR < $1M; for ARR >= $1M the cap should be 2% of annualized commit.

Also want clarity on credit escrow governance (who holds it and how refunds are documented).

If Redwood can accept a modest extension to 4 months and adjust the cap to a tiered structure, we should be able to sign quickly.

—Tom
VP Legal, Stellaris Health

From: irene_choi@redwood-inference.com
To: Tom Nguyen <t.nguyen@stellarishealth.com>, Emma L. Harper <emma.harper@stellarishealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com, marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Final approach — compromise terms and next steps

Tom / Emma —

Appreciate the quick turn. After a final review with Finance and Legal, Redwood can accept the following compromise to close the order: 

- Measurement Start Date: October 1, 2027 (initial year only).
- Temporary floor suspension: four (4) months from Service Activation, provided Appendix A milestones are met or delayed by documented third-party vendor issues (the buffer is limited to vendor-caused delays only).
- Surcharge cap: adopt tiered cap as proposed — $25,000 cap if first-year ARR < $1M; otherwise 2% of annualized commit for ARR >= $1M.
- Credits escrow: Redwood will hold the $10,000 credit on account with a simple refund/credit note issued at true-up. Documentation of escrow governance will be included in Section 5 of the Pricing Exhibit.

Marissa: please issue a clean Pricing Exhibit and updated Order Form (v3) reflecting the agreed edits. Karthik: once Marissa circulates the final doc, Emma please confirm and we will send for signature.

If the above matches Stellaris' internal approvals Emma / Tom, let's aim to execute within 5 business days so onboarding can start on schedule.

Thanks —
Irene
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Stellaris_OrderForm_v3.pdf
